_note: Prepared Second Chair analyses for the SYNTHETIC demo matter. Every quote must exist verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in the cited document; demo/build.py refuses to build otherwise. No legal authority is cited: authority comes only from the Legal research leads workflow.
issues: maintain product between 2 and 8 degrees temperature excursion
notify temperature excursion within two hours of detection
liability limitation per shipment gross negligence
cargo claim insurer denied late notice

plaintiff.theory: Meridian let the April 12 load on trailer 4471 run warm for hours, told no one until morning, and knew the compressor was failing. Harbor Point lost all 22 pallets and is owed the full USD 412,500.

arguments.title: Meridian broke the temperature promise on the April 12 load
arguments.text: The MSA requires Meridian to hold product between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius at all times. The trailer's recorder, the shipment log and Meridian's own witness all show readings far above that range for hours.

cites.quote: Meridian shall maintain product between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius at all times.
L00144 2023-04-12 4471 Stockton Sacramento 3.4 11.4 YES - high
Yes. The recorder showed 11.4 degrees for about three hours.

arguments.title: Meridian gave no notice for roughly five hours
arguments.text: Section 7.3 requires notice within two hours of detection. Meridian's driver reset the unit at 2:10 AM, so the excursion was known on the road, yet the first notice is Meridian's 7:02 AM email. Meridian's dispatch director admits the alarm went to an unmonitored inbox.

cites.quote: Meridian shall notify Harbor Point of any Temperature Excursion within two hours of detection.
Driver Tomas Ferreira reset the unit at 2:10 AM.
No. Our dispatcher was off shift and the alarm went to an unmonitored inbox.
Not until the next morning, April 13. Nobody called me that night.

arguments.title: The loss flows directly from the excursion
arguments.text: Section 8 makes Meridian liable for loss caused by a Temperature Excursion. The consignee rejected the entire load and wrote the temperature reading on the receipt as the reason.

cites.quote: Meridian is liable for loss or damage to Product caused by a Temperature Excursion, subject to Section 9.
Consignee REJECTED 22 pallets.
Reason: reefer temperature 11.4 C above limit.

arguments.title: The USD 250,000 cap falls away for gross negligence
arguments.text: The cap has an express gross-negligence exception. Meridian's own maintenance ticket (Bates HPCS-000412) shows the 4471 compressor was flagged in February and its replacement deferred; Meridian kept the trailer in service and routed alarms to an inbox nobody watched.

cites.quote: Liability per shipment shall not exceed USD 250,000 except for gross negligence.
Maintenance ticket: compressor on trailer 4471 flagged for replacement in February 2023, deferred.
the compressor on 4471 was flagged in February maintenance and never replaced.
the alarm went to an unmonitored inbox.

arguments.title: Meridian was already on notice from the March 4410 excursion
arguments.text: A month earlier, another Meridian trailer ran warm past the 30-minute threshold and Harbor Point complained in writing that the two-hour notice never came. Meridian cannot call April 12 a one-off.

cites.quote: trailer 4410 recorder shows a 42-minute excursion to 9.1C on March 13 near Lodi.
we did not receive the two-hour notice required by Section 7.3 for the 4410 excursion.

arguments.title: The claim was timely, and Meridian's insurance promise is in play
arguments.text: Harbor Point submitted its written claim on May 2, well inside the 90-day window. Meridian had to insure the cargo with Harbor Point as loss payee; its insurer then denied the claim for late notice, which was Meridian's own failure.

cites.quote: Claims must be submitted in writing within ninety days of delivery.
attached is our cargo claim for USD 412,500 for the April 12 load.
Meridian shall carry cargo insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence naming Harbor Point as loss payee.
our insurer denied the claim citing late notice under the policy.
